Deich.et:
From Middle Low German dīk, from Old Saxon dīk, from Proto-West Germanic *dīk, from Proto-Germanic *dīkaz.
Originally the same word as Teich (“pond”). The sense “dike” spread via Low German, for which reason the form Deich is most often regarded as an artifici…

Deichsel.et: From Middle High German dīhsel, from Old High German dīhsala, from Proto-West Germanic *þīhslu, from Proto-Germanic *þinhslō.

deinetwegen.et: Shortened from von deinetwegen, which can be traced through two developmental routes. One route is from von deinentwegen / von deinent wegen, from von deinen wegen, from Middle High German von dînen wegen, in which wegen was the dative plural of modern-day Weg…

Deibel.et: Regional forms of Teufel (“devil”); in the case of Deibel: East Central German. These have spread supraregionally, possibly due to the fact that mentioning the devil’s name was considered obscene (for religious or superstitious reasons).

s: from your lips to God's ears; expresses that the speaker wants a preceding statement to be true, but considers it doubtful or even unlikely in most cases there is no unlikely element. It is just a hope (prayer) that the statement come true.

deinesgleichen.et: deines (genitive case of personal pronoun 2 sg) + gleich (“similar, equal”)

Deichschart.et: From Deich (“dyke”) + Low German Schart (“notch, cleft”), a partial calque of Low German Diekscha(a)rt n, from Middle Low German dîk + schārt.

Deichgraf.et: From Deich + Graf, compare Dutch dijkgraaf.
